Answer on the 48 s reverse queries: yes, that is the expected shape of today's target-scoped reverse design on Vector, not a regression, and two levers exist, one cheap.
1. Why 48 s. A sink such as `std.io.Stdout.write` is bound by a reverse query (call-sites-to the modeled declaration): discovery by NAME over the per-blob inventory (every `write`, `write_all`, `info`, ... occurrence in Vector), then forward confirmation per candidate blob (rust_selected::reverse_confirm_blob: 3,087 calls over 52 queries, about 59 blobs per query, 232 ms each), and each confirmation needs a receiver-type proof (rust_caller::register_and_resolve 9,223 calls, 110 ms each, the same ~115 ms per receiver proof I attributed earlier). #3828's target scoping narrows gaps, not candidates with common names, so cost = candidate blobs for the name x receiver-proof cost. Nothing in the parked call-target work (forward batches) or #4664 (occurrence targets) touches this path; #4616/#4626 only touch the forward resolve_call_target_batch share (329 s here).
2. Cheap lever, worth one experiment: the seek storm is mostly syscalls because reader connections use an 8 MiB page cache with mmap disabled (crates/bifrost-core/src/cache_db.rs: READER_PAGE_CACHE_KIB = -8192 at ~969, mmap_size 0 at ~989; streaming readers 2 MiB). On a 1.6 GB cache every seek outside that window is a read(), matching your 1,165 s sys and 70% in sqlite3BtreeIndexMoveto. The comment there records the trade-off measured on a smaller tree and the pcache mutex reason (BrokkAi/bifrost#21) for no mmap. Try a whole-workspace run with the reader page cache at 512 MiB-1 GiB (or mmap on for a read-only whole-workspace run) and compare sys time and wall; the host has 98 GB. If it helps, the fix is a per-role budget for whole-workspace runs, not a global change.
3. Design lever (mine, after the agent switch): prune reverse candidates by receiver-type family before confirmation. selected_reverse.rs already knows type-bound receivers (~274 `binding.type_bound_receiver()`, receiver-analysis budget ~461-475) but discovery is name-only; a per-blob typed discovery row (the chapter's typed layer applied to reverse search) would let `Stdout.write` skip the thousands of `write` calls on other receivers. I will take that as a design item.
4. For the demo, your M4 direction (changed-range sinks, sources matched lazily on the frontier) avoids workspace-wide reverse selection entirely; the reverse cost matters for whole-workspace mode and oracle captures. Send me the policy file, commands and harness path; I will run the page-cache experiment once my lanes are on the new backend.

The resolution session is adding the missing activation data, and I've accepted their design. Their new reader gives each caller file one of three verdicts:

- **Active:** at least one placement is compiled in the selected configuration. Test-target placements count.
- **Inactive:** no placement is active, and every route that would place the file has a recorded `activation=0`.
- **Unknown:** anything else, such as a file with no cfg evidence.

Composition will skip only Inactive files. Unknown files are explored exactly as they are today, with no new incompleteness marker. That way a file without cfg evidence is never dropped silently.

I asked them to check one thing in their lane. The Vector Windows tests file that caused the 24 extra solves must come out as Inactive. If it reads Unknown, the filter won't help the demo at all.
